record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: A semi-dispersive billiard table is obtained from a polygon by replacing some sides by smooth boundary components that are convex inward, while any remaining straight sides are neutral components; a semi-dispersive polygon is the special case where the dispersive components are circular arcs. Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic? Is every semi-dispersive polygon hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: These are the semi-dispersive billiard tables. In the absence of neutral components, we speak of dispersive billiard tables.
Problem 4. i) Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic? ii) Is every semi-dispersive polygon hyperbolic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A planar billiard table is a compact connected region $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ whose boundary $\partial Q$ consists of finitely many smooth arcs. The billiard flow is the motion of a point particle inside $Q$ at unit speed, reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at boundary points where $\partial Q$ is smooth. A boundary component is called dispersive if it is smooth and strictly convex when viewed from inside $Q$ (i.e., curves away from the interior); it is called neutral if it is a straight line segment. 

A semi-dispersive billiard table is one obtained from a polygon $P$ by replacing some of its sides by smooth boundary arcs that are dispersive (convex inward), while the remaining sides are kept as straight (neutral) segments. A semi-dispersive polygon is the special case in which every dispersive component is a circular arc.

The billiard map (boundary map) is hyperbolic if at almost every phase point all Lyapunov exponents of the billiard map are nonzero.

Questions. 
(i) Is every semi-dispersive billiard table (in the sense above) hyperbolic? 
(ii) Is every semi-dispersive polygon hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: Hyperbolicity is established for various classical sub-classes of semi-dispersive billiards (e.g., Sinai-type dispersive billiards, hard-sphere systems, certain rational-polygon-based reflection constructions, and stadium-like models). However, the general questions of whether every semi-dispersive billiard table, and every semi-dispersive polygon, are hyperbolic do not appear to have been resolved in the literature; they are listed as open problems in recent surveys on billiard dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Hard Ball Systems and Semi-Dispersive Billiards: Hyperbolicity and Ergodicity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of hyperbolicity/ergodicity results for semi-dispersive billiards, with hyperbolicity proved only in particular settings.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity of semi-dispersive billiards is known in special cases but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Billiards and Statistical Physics (Chernov–Dolgopyat)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing classes of billiards known to be hyperbolic and outstanding problems.
status_evidence.claim: General hyperbolicity questions for semi-dispersive tables remain open.

status_evidence.title: Bridge to Hyperbolic Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Studies polygonal billiards modified by curved (dispersive) sides and conditions yielding hyperbolicity.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity in semi-dispersive polygons is studied but not established in full generality.
